Why is Redis 100x faster than MySQL?
In this 15-second deep dive, we compare:
• RAM vs NVMe Disk access latency (100ns vs 100,000ns)
• Single-threaded event loop (epoll / kqueue) vs Multi-threaded lock contention
• Cache-aside architectural pattern for 10x throughput

📌 Recommended Architecture:
Keep MySQL as your persistent source of truth (ACID compliance) and layer Redis as an in-memory cache-aside buffer to absorb 95% of read queries.

insta_caption:
Why is Redis 100x faster than MySQL? 🚀⚡

It comes down to 2 engineering fundamentals:
1️⃣ RAM vs Disk latency: Memory access takes ~100ns, while NVMe SSD random reads take ~100,000ns.
2️⃣ Single-Threaded Event Loop: Redis eliminates lock contention and thread context switching using Linux epoll.

Pro Tip: Never replace MySQL with Redis. Use Redis as a cache-aside buffer and MySQL as your persistent store of truth!
